What this means for your business

A neighbor should be able to find the right hours, understand what you sell, and act without hunting through five apps. Your website is the place you control; profiles and social pages point toward it.

What to watch

  • Different hours or phone numbers across listings.
  • A homepage that never says what the business does.
  • A booking, menu, or order link that disappears on a phone.
  • A social account acting as the only source of truth.

Do this next

  1. Claim and verify the Google Business Profile.
  2. Make the name, address, phone, hours, and services match everywhere.
  3. Test the full customer path on a phone.
  4. Fix the first dead end before adding another channel.

When Little Fight fits

We help when the website, listings, forms, bookings, and follow-up need to work together. If one wrong hour is the whole problem, fix the hour first. You do not need a big project for that.

Get a plain-English second opinion

insight.answer: You need three things to agree: your business details, your website, and the next action a customer should take. More channels do not fix a broken path.
